dataset.description: Semi-structured interviews with various stakeholders, such as manufacturers, regulatory bodies, environmental NGOs, and academic experts.

distribution.title:
The objective is to gather qualitative data about their experiences, perceptions, and insights regarding the regulatory landscape for biodegradable materials.
Through direct interviews, postdoctoral reasearcher will explore stakeholders’ views on the existing regulations, identifying areas they perceive as overly restrictive or insufficiently robust. This dialogue will not only allow for the identification of regulatory gaps but will also uncover specific challenges faced in the practical application of biodegradable packaging within diverse industrial contexts. Stakeholder perspectives are integral to understanding the real-world implications of regulations, and their input will be instrumental in shaping our research findings.
The outcomes of these interviews will be synthesised into a comprehensive stakeholder report, highlighting common challenges, innovative practices, and regulatory suggestions.

dmp.description:
Currently, research into self-biodegradable materials is in its infancy, with the first studies only now emerging globally. This makes it an emerging industry with no existing regulatory framework, positioning the project as a cutting-edge industrial research initiative.
During the project, the first-ever scientifically validated roadmap (algorithm) for determining the shelf life of self-biodegradable packaging materials will be developed. The self-biodegradability process is distinct from general biodegradability, and therefore, life-cycle assessment methods differ accordingly. As these materials begin to emerge globally, there is a complete lack of technical standards and legal criteria defining how long such packaging remains effective and safe for use in food and other industries.
This project aims to fill that gap by establishing practical, measurable indicators for shelf-life determination, grounded in interdisciplinary research and aligned with both industrial applications and regulatory needs. The outcome will serve as an AI-compatible decision-support tool for packaging developers, manufacturers, and regulators, enabling integration into artificial intelligence systems for automated expiry assessment. In doing so, the project will contribute to sustainability, compliance, and innovation in the packaging sector, with a particular focus on food and other industries with the highest safety requirements.
